subject: ENGLISH
title: Yesterday, Today, Tomorrow · M01 D12
objective: Use simple regular verbs for past, present, and future time.
introduction: Yesterday Milo walked, today he walks, and tomorrow he will walk! Match each verb to its time.

vocabulary.definition: The time that has already happened.
The time that is still to come.

activities.instruction: See how verbs change for past, present, and future!
activities.content: Regular past verbs often use -ed; present forms depend on the subject; future can use will plus the base verb.

feedback.retry: Use the time word to choose a past, present, or future verb form. 💪

items.prompt: Which sentence is about the past?
items.explanation: “Yesterday” is a past clue, and walked ends in -ed, so this sentence is about the past. “Will walk” is for the future, and “tomorrow” with “walked yesterday” is mixed up.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses its time clue correctly?
items.explanation: Yesterday is past and walked has -ed, so the pair fits. “Will walk” is future, and “tomorrow” does not go with “walked yesterday.”

items.prompt: Which sentence mixes up its time clue?
items.explanation: “Yesterday we will walk” is mixed up: yesterday is past, but will walk is future. The other sentences match their time clues.

items.prompt: Which sentence is about the future?
items.explanation: “Will visit” tells about tomorrow, so it is the future. “Visited” is past, and “visit” is present.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses the right verb for the time?
items.explanation: Tomorrow is future, so “will walk” fits. “He walk” needs -s for he, and “yesterday” cannot go with “will walk.”
